title: Notice, Records and Runout Standards: Member Appeals Program
content:
The notices, record keeping, runout period and service complaints of the Member Appeals Program are governed by five standards, each set for every Northbridge Appeals package. Four of them are the same in all six packages; one differs.

## Standards that are the same in all six packages

1. **Language assistance threshold: 10 percent.** Notices carry a statement of language assistance in a non-English language when the share of a county's population that is literate only in that language reaches 10 percent.
2. **Runout period: 180 calendar days.** After the coverage end date, the appeal program stays in runout for 180 calendar days, so denials from covered dates can still be appealed.
3. **Record retention: 6 years.** Appeal case files are kept for 6 years.
4. **Service complaints: 30 calendar days.** A service complaint that is not an appeal of a denial is resolved within 30 calendar days.

## The standard that differs: naming the state consumer assistance program

| Package | Denial notice names the state consumer assistance program |
|---|---|
| Northbridge Appeals Level One Delegated | No |
| Northbridge Appeals Two-Level Delegated | No |
| Northbridge Appeals Single-Level with External Review | No |
| Northbridge Appeals Two-Level with External Review | No |
| Northbridge Appeals State-Regulated Insured | Yes |
| Northbridge Appeals Full Fiduciary Delegation | No |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- *Language assistance.* In a county where 10 percent of the population is literate only in one non-English language, the threshold is met, and notices carry the language assistance statement in that language. At 9 percent the threshold is not met.
- *Runout.* A member's plan coverage ended on 31 March. Under any package, the program is in runout for 180 calendar days after that coverage end date.
